# InstanceDeck

> Multi-instance app launcher for Windows. Free and open source under MIT.

InstanceDeck launches official installed apps with per-profile arguments, environment variables and data paths. It does not modify target binaries, read credentials or collect telemetry. Profiles are not a security sandbox.

Current status: development. Guided Claude sign-in has synthetic crash-test coverage; real account verification is pending. Windows shell integration is implemented with pinning verification pending. Eight built-in recipes, custom app configuration, metadata import/export, optional Codex sessions sharing and dark theme are implemented. All built-in recipes remain Community while manual account smoke testing is deferred. Recipe status does not imply verified account identity.

## Recipes

- [Brave](https://tanzir71.github.io/instancedeck/apps/brave/) — community: InstanceDeck launches the installed Brave executable with a separate data directory. The recipe uses app launch settings and leaves binaries untouched. Verify each visible account and data path before use.
- [Claude Desktop](https://tanzir71.github.io/instancedeck/apps/claude-desktop/) — community: Claude Desktop profiles use a separate user-data directory and LOCALAPPDATA so each launch has its own state. Windows sends browser sign-in callbacks to the main app, so new accounts need a guided snapshot sign-in.
- [Codex](https://tanzir71.github.io/instancedeck/apps/codex/) — community: Codex profiles set CODEX_HOME and CODEX_ELECTRON_USER_DATA_PATH before launching the official Store app. This separates desktop state and CLI sessions; check the visible account in every profile after an update.
- [Cursor](https://tanzir71.github.io/instancedeck/apps/cursor/) — community: InstanceDeck launches the installed Cursor executable with a separate data directory. The recipe uses app launch settings and leaves binaries untouched. Verify each visible account and data path before use.
- [Google Chrome](https://tanzir71.github.io/instancedeck/apps/chrome/) — community: InstanceDeck launches the installed Google Chrome executable with a separate data directory. The recipe uses app launch settings and leaves binaries untouched. Verify each visible account and data path before use.
- [Microsoft Edge](https://tanzir71.github.io/instancedeck/apps/edge/) — community: InstanceDeck launches the installed Microsoft Edge executable with a separate data directory. The recipe uses app launch settings and leaves binaries untouched. Verify each visible account and data path before use.
- [Telegram Desktop](https://tanzir71.github.io/instancedeck/apps/telegram-desktop/) — community: InstanceDeck launches the installed Telegram Desktop executable with a separate data directory. The recipe uses app launch settings and leaves binaries untouched. Verify each visible account and data path before use.
- [Visual Studio Code](https://tanzir71.github.io/instancedeck/apps/vscode/) — community: InstanceDeck launches the installed Visual Studio Code executable with a separate data directory. The recipe uses app launch settings and leaves binaries untouched. Verify each visible account and data path before use.
